You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The pattern points to a period when headline CPI had fallen sharply, the 2-year yield had risen strongly, the dollar was very strong, payrolls were very strong, and the unemployment rate was low.

Headline CPI at -3.0 with a 3-month change of -2.5 suggests an energy price collapse. The 2-year yield z-score of +2.5 against a policy rate z-score of 0 suggests the 2-year had risen well above its 3-year average while the policy rate was near its average. The dollar at +2.5 fits 2014-2015 or late 2024 to 2025.

Late 2014 to early 2015 fits the energy collapse, but the policy rate then was near zero, and a z-score of 0 against the prior 36 months of near-zero rates is plausible. The 2-year yield z-score of +2.5 is less obvious for that period, though. Payrolls were strong in early 2015. The dollar was surging. The 10-year yield z-score of -0.5 would fit, and the 10y-2y spread falling fits too. Core CPI at -1.0 also fits.

The 2-year z-score of +2.5 with a 12-month change of +1.5 fits 2015, as the 2-year rose from about 0.4% to 0.7% by late 2014 and 2015. Over the prior 36 months it had been 0.2-0.5%, so a rise to about 0.7% in early-to-mid 2015 gives a high z. The policy rate z of 0 with a 3-month change of +0.5 fits December 2015 to early 2016, when the first hike occurred. The 2-year was about 1.0% in December 2015, the dollar was at its peak, and CPI was low. Unemployment z of -1.5 fits a rate of 5.0%. The 1-month equity return of +1.5 fits November 2015 (+0.3%) less well, and the 1-month return in October 2015 was +8%. A 1-month Treasury return of -1.5 fits November 2015, when the 2-year jumped. The 12-month equity return of -0.5 fits 2015 as a flat year. Emerging markets had a 6-month return of -1.5, which fits after the August 2015 selloff.

The best fit is November or December 2015. I'd pick December 2015, because the policy rate's 3-month change of +0.5 suggests the hike was already in the data, and equities were down in December. The 1-month equity return of +1.5 favours November, when the S&P was up about 0.3% and developed ex-US was up slightly. Treasuries fell in November, as the figures show. I'll go with November 2015.
